questions.question: An object moves along a straight path for 5 s. Its initial velocity is 10 m s ⁻¹ and its final velocity is -2 m s ⁻¹ . What is the magnitude of the average velocity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4 m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **initial velocity** (**u**) of the object is given as **10 m/s**. This represents the velocity at the start of the **5-second** time interval.
 
• The **final velocity** (**v**) of the object is given as **-2 m/s**. The **negative sign** indicates that the object is moving in the **opposite direction** to its initial motion at the end of the time period.
 
• The object moves along a **straight path**, which allows us to use **linear kinematic equations** to determine its motion parameters.
 
• For an object moving with **uniform acceleration**, the **average velocity** is calculated using the formula: **Average Velocity = (u + v) / 2**.
 
• Substituting the given values into the formula: **(10 + (-2)) / 2 = 8 / 2 = 4 m/s**.
 
• The question asks for the **magnitude** of the average velocity. The magnitude is the **absolute value**, which is **4 m/s**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 4 m/s.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Velocity as a Vector Quantity:** 
 
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity** because it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**. In this problem, the change from **positive** to **negative** velocity signifies a reversal in direction.
 
 
 
• **Average Velocity vs. Average Speed:**
 
 
• **Average Velocity** is defined as the **total displacement** divided by the **total time** taken.
 
• **Average Speed** is the **total distance** traveled divided by the time. If the object reversed direction, the distance would be greater than the displacement, making average speed higher than the magnitude of average velocity.
 
 
 
• **SI Units:**
 
 
• The standard **International System of Units (SI)** for velocity is **meters per second (m/s)**. Other common units include **km/h** or **miles per hour**, but physics calculations typically require conversion to **m/s**.
 
 
 
• **Displacement Calculation:**
 
 
• Since **Average Velocity = Displacement / Time**, we can find the total **displacement** by multiplying the average velocity (**4 m/s**) by the time (**5 s**), resulting in a displacement of **20 meters**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Uniform Acceleration:** The formula **(u + v) / 2** is strictly applicable when the object undergoes **constant acceleration**. If the acceleration varied non-linearly over the **5 seconds**, this simple arithmetic mean would not represent the true average velocity.
 
• **Sign Convention:** In **one-dimensional motion**, signs (+ or -) are used to denote direction. A **negative final velocity** implies the object decelerated to zero and then accelerated in the **reverse direction**.
 
• **Magnitude:** When a question asks for "magnitude," it specifically requires the **numerical value** without the directional sign. Even if the calculation resulted in a negative value, the magnitude remains **positive**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT the correct use of a concave mirror?

options.text: It is used as a shaving mirror.
It is used as a rear view mirror in automobiles.
It is used in a solar furnace.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is used as a rear view mirror in automobiles.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave mirror** is a spherical mirror with an inwardly curved reflecting surface that **converges** light rays. It is widely used in various applications due to its ability to form **magnified** and **real** images depending on the distance of the object.
 
• **Shaving Mirrors**: When an object is placed very close to a **concave mirror** (between the **principal focus** and the **pole**), it produces an **erect**, **virtual**, and highly **magnified** image of the face. This allows for a better and closer view during shaving. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Torches and Searchlights**: In these devices, the light source (bulb) is placed at the **focus** of the **concave mirror**. The light rays emerging from the bulb hit the mirror and are reflected as a **powerful parallel beam of light** that can travel long distances. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Rear View Mirrors**: For **automobiles**, **convex mirrors** are used as rear-view mirrors, not concave mirrors. **Convex mirrors** are preferred because they always form an **erect** (upright) though **diminished** image and provide a much **wider field of view**, allowing the driver to see a large area of traffic behind them. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Solar Furnaces**: Large **concave mirrors** are utilized to capture and **concentrate** parallel sun rays at a single **focal point**. This concentration of solar energy produces an intense amount of **heat**, which is used for industrial or experimental heating purposes. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is It is used as a rear view mirror in automobiles.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Spherical Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Concave Mirror:** Also known as a **converging mirror**. It can produce both **real** and **virtual** images. When the object is far, the image is **inverted**; when the object is very close, the image is **upright** and **enlarged**.
 
• **Convex Mirror:** Also known as a **diverging mirror**. It always forms a **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished** image, regardless of the object's distance from the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Image Characteristics:**
 
 
• A **real image** is formed when light rays actually meet at a point and can be obtained on a **screen**.
 
• A **virtual image** is formed when light rays appear to meet behind the mirror and cannot be caught on a screen.
 
 
 
• **Common Applications:**
 
 
• **Dentist Mirrors:** Dentists use **concave mirrors** to see a **magnified image** of the teeth to identify cavities or issues clearly.
 
• **Headlights:** Car **headlights** use concave reflectors to send out **parallel rays** of light for better visibility at night.
 
• **Security Mirrors:** Large **convex mirrors** are used in shops and **blind turns** on roads to provide a **wide-angle view** for safety and surveillance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:** The relationship between **object distance (u)**, **image distance (v)**, and **focal length (f)** is given by the formula **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **New Cartesian Sign Convention**, the **focal length** of a **concave mirror** is always **negative**, while the focal length of a **convex mirror** is always **positive**.
 
• **Magnification (m):** It is the ratio of the height of the image to the height of the object. For a **concave mirror**, **m** can be greater than, equal to, or less than **1**. For a **convex mirror**, **m** is always **less than 1**.
 
• **Pole and Principal Axis:** The geometric center of the reflecting surface is called the **pole (P)**, and the straight line passing through the pole and the **center of curvature (C)** is the **principal axis**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following causes a change in the state of matter?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Changing temperature or pressure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Matter** can exist in different states, primarily **solid**, **liquid**, and **gas**. The state of a substance is determined by the **kinetic energy** of its particles and the **intermolecular forces** of attraction between them.
 
• **Changing temperature** is a primary cause of state change. When heat is added, particles gain **kinetic energy** and move faster, eventually breaking the bonds of the **solid** or **liquid** state to transition into a more fluid or gaseous form. Conversely, removing heat slows down particles.
 
• **Changing pressure** also alters the state of matter by forcing particles closer together or allowing them to spread apart. For example, increasing **pressure** on a gas can compress it into a **liquid** state. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Cutting a substance** only changes its **physical dimensions** (size and shape) but does not alter the arrangement of atoms or the phase of the matter. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Mixing it with another substance** generally creates a **mixture** or a **chemical compound**, but it is not a direct physical mechanism for changing the inherent state of a pure substance. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Dissolving a substance** (like salt in water) involves breaking the substance into **ions** or **molecules** within a **solvent** to form a **solution**, which is a physical process rather than a phase transition of the substance itself into a liquid. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Phase Transitions:**
 
 
• **Melting**: The process where a **solid** turns into a **liquid** due to an increase in **temperature**. The specific temperature is known as the **Melting Point**.
 
• **Vaporization**: The transition from a **liquid** to a **gas**. This includes **boiling** (throughout the liquid) and **evaporation** (at the surface).
 
• **Condensation**: The change of state from **gas** to **liquid**, usually occurring when the **temperature** drops.
 
• **Freezing**: The transition from **liquid** to **solid**. The **Freezing Point** of water is **0 degrees Celsius** or **273.15 Kelvin**.
 
 
 
• **Sublimation and Deposition:**
 
 
• **Sublimation**: A rare process where a **solid** changes directly into a **gas** without passing through the liquid phase. Examples include **Dry Ice** (solid **CO2**) and **Naphthalene** balls.
 
• **Deposition**: The direct transition from a **gas** to a **solid**, such as the formation of **frost** on a cold surface.
 
 
 
• **The Role of Latent Heat:**
 
 
• During a change of state, the **temperature** of a substance remains **constant** even though heat is being supplied. This heat is known as **Latent Heat**, which is used to overcome **intermolecular forces** rather than increasing the **kinetic energy** of the particles.
 
 
 
• **Effect of Pressure on Gases:**
 
 
• Gases are highly **compressible**. By applying **high pressure** and reducing **temperature**, gases like **Oxygen** and **Nitrogen** can be **liquefied** for industrial and medical use. **LPG** (Liquefied Petroleum Gas) is a common example of a gas stored as a liquid under **high pressure**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Triple Point**: The specific **temperature** and **pressure** at which the **solid**, **liquid**, and **gaseous** phases of a substance coexist in **thermodynamic equilibrium**.
 
• **Critical Point**: The **temperature** and **pressure** beyond which the distinction between **liquid** and **gas** phases disappears, resulting in a **supercritical fluid**.
 
• **Plasma**: Considered the **fourth state of matter**, it consists of **super-heated**, **ionized gas** and is found in **stars** and **neon signs**.
</ul

questions.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the microscopic observation of onion peel cells?

options.text: The size of the onion decides the shape of its individual cells
All onions are made up of similar small structures called cells
Onion bulbs contain different cell types for different functions
Each onion peel contains cells of different composition

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All onions are made up of similar small structures called cells**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The microscopic observation of **onion peel** (the **epidermis**) demonstrates that all onions, regardless of their **size**, **shape**, or **variety**, are composed of basic structural units known as **cells**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• When an onion peel is examined under a **compound microscope**, it reveals a pattern of **rectangular** or **brick-shaped** compartments arranged in a regular fashion, each containing a **nucleus** and **cytoplasm**.
 
• The **size** of the onion bulb does not affect the **shape** or **size** of these individual cells; a large onion and a small onion will both show identical-looking cellular structures under magnification. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **onion peel** is a **homogenous tissue** layer (the **protective epidermis**), meaning the cells within this specific layer are very similar in **composition** and **function**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• While an entire **onion plant** has different cell types for different functions (such as **root cells** or **vascular cells**), the specific observation of the **peel** primarily highlights the **uniformity** of the **dermal tissue** rather than a diversity of functions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of an Onion Cell:** As a typical **plant cell**, an onion cell contains a **rigid cell wall** made of **cellulose**, which provides **structural support**. It also features a large **central vacuole** that maintains **turgor pressure** and pushes the **nucleus** to the **periphery**.
 
• **The Role of Staining:** Because most cell organelles are **transparent**, stains like **Safranin** or **Iodine solution** are used. These **chemicals** color the **nucleus** and **cell wall** more intensely, making them clearly visible under **light microscopy**.
 
• **Cell Theory:** The observation of onion cells is a fundamental piece of evidence for the **Cell Theory**, formulated by **Matthias Schleiden** and **Theodor Schwann** in **1838-1839**. This theory states that **all living things** are made of **cells** and cells are the **basic unit of life**.
 
• **Historical Context:** The term "cell" was first coined by **Robert Hooke** in **1665** after observing **cork**. Later, in **1831**, **Robert Brown** discovered the **nucleus** within the plant cell, which is easily seen in onion peel preparations.
 
• **Onion Bulb Botany:** The **onion** (***Allium cepa***) is a **modified underground stem** called a **bulb**. The "peels" we observe are the **epidermal layers** of the fleshy **leaves** that store **food** and **nutrients** for the plant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Experimental Procedure:** To observe these cells, a thin **transparent membrane** is stripped from the **concave side** of an onion fleshy scale. It is placed in a **watch glass** with **water** to prevent **dehydration** or **folding**.
 
• **Mounting:** The specimen is mounted on a **glass slide** with a drop of **glycerin** (to prevent drying) and covered with a **coverslip**. It is vital to avoid **air bubbles** during this process for a clear **microscopic view**.
 
• **Magnification:** Typical classroom observations use a **low-power objective** (**10x**) for a wide field of view and a **high-power objective** (**40x**) to see the **nucleus** and **cell boundaries** in detail.
 
• **Biological Classification:** Onions are **monocotyledons**, and their cells are often used in labs because they are large, easy to extract, and provide a **single-layer** view of **eukaryotic** architecture.

questions.question: What type of force is responsible for the Moon’s circular motion around Earth?

options.text: Centripetal Force due to Earth's gravity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centripetal Force due to Earth's gravity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **circular motion** of the **Moon** around the **Earth** is primarily maintained by **Centripetal Force**, which is a "center-seeking" force directed toward the center of the orbit.
 
• In the case of the Earth-Moon system, this necessary centripetal force is provided by the **gravitational attraction** exerted by the **Earth** on the **Moon**. Without this force, the Moon would move in a straight line tangent to its orbit due to **inertia**.
 
• According to **Sir Isaac Newton's** laws, an object in motion will remain in motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force. Gravity acts as this external force, constantly pulling the Moon toward the **Earth** and changing its **velocity vector** direction at every point.
 
• While the force changes the **direction** of the Moon's movement, it does not change its **orbital speed** (assuming a perfectly circular orbit). This results in a continuous **centripetal acceleration** directed toward the Earth's center. ***Hence, the correct answer is Centripetal Force due to Earth's gravity.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**:
 
 
• The force of gravity between two bodies is proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the **square of the distance** between their centers.
 
• The average distance between the **Earth** and the **Moon** is approximately **384,400 kilometers**. The **mass** of the Moon is about **7.347 x 10^22 kg**, while the Earth is about **5.972 x 10^24 kg**.
 
 
 
• **Centrifugal Force vs. Centripetal Force**:
 
 
• **Centripetal force** is a real force acting toward the center. In contrast, **Centrifugal force** is an **apparent** or **fictitious force** that appears to act outward when observed from a **rotating frame of reference**.
 
• In the Earth-Moon system, from the Moon's perspective (a non-inertial frame), it feels an outward centrifugal force that balances the inward gravitational pull, maintaining **orbital equilibrium**.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Other Forces**:
 
 
• **Normal Force**: This is a **contact force** exerted by a surface perpendicular to an object resting on it. Since the Moon and Earth are separated by the vacuum of space, no normal force is involved.
 
• **Electromagnetic Force**: While this force is much stronger than gravity at a microscopic level, celestial bodies are generally **electrically neutral**. Therefore, **gravity** is the dominant force governing large-scale planetary motion.
 
 
 
• **Tidal Effects**:
 
 
• The gravitational interaction is mutual. While Earth keeps the Moon in orbit, the **Moon's gravity** pulls on Earth's oceans, causing **high tides** and **low tides**. This interaction also leads to **tidal locking**, which is why we always see the same side of the Moon.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Orbital Velocity**: For the Moon to remain in a stable orbit, it must maintain a specific **orbital velocity** of about **1.022 km/s**. If the velocity were too high, it would escape into space; if it were too low, it would crash into the Earth.
 
• **Kepler's Laws**: Although we often simplify the orbit as circular, **Johannes Kepler** proved in **1609** that planetary orbits are **elliptical**, with the central body at one focus. The Moon's orbit has an **eccentricity** of about **0.0549**.
 
• **History**: The realization that the same force making an apple fall to the ground also keeps the Moon in its orbit was a revolutionary insight published in **Newton's Principia Mathematica** in **1687**.
</ul

questions.question: If a piece of aluminium is added to iron(II) sulphate ( FeSO₄ ) solution, what will happen?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Iron will get deposited**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction between **Aluminium (Al)** and **Iron(II) sulphate (FeSO4)** is a classic example of a **displacement reaction**. In such reactions, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• According to the **reactivity series** of metals, **Aluminium** is positioned higher than **Iron**. This indicates that **Aluminium** is **chemically more reactive** than **Iron** and has a stronger tendency to lose electrons and form ions.
 
• When **Aluminium** pieces are added to a solution of **Iron(II) sulphate**, the **Aluminium** atoms displace the **Iron** ions from the solution. The chemical equation for this reaction is: **2Al (s) + 3FeSO4 (aq) → Al2(SO4)3 (aq) + 3Fe (s)**.
 
• As a result of this displacement, solid **Iron** metal is liberated and begins to settle or **deposit** on the surface of the **Aluminium** or at the bottom of the container. ***Hence, the statement that iron will get deposited is correct.***
 
• During the process, the **light green** color of the **Iron(II) sulphate** solution fades away, and the solution eventually becomes **colorless** due to the formation of **Aluminium sulphate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reactivity Series of Metals:**
 
 
• The **reactivity series** is a list of metals arranged in the **decreasing order** of their chemical reactivity. Metals like **Potassium (K)** and **Sodium (Na)** are at the top, while **Gold (Au)** and **Platinum (Pt)** are at the bottom.
 
• **Aluminium** has an **atomic number** of **13** and is known for its low density and high resistance to **corrosion** due to the formation of a protective **oxide layer**.
 
• **Iron** has an **atomic number** of **26**. In **FeSO4**, iron exists in the **+2 oxidation state** (Ferrous).
 
 
 
• **Properties of Iron(II) Sulphate (FeSO4):**
 
 
• It is commonly known as **Green Vitriol** or **Copperas**.
 
• In its **heptahydrate** form (**FeSO4·7H2O**), it appears as **blue-green** crystals. In an aqueous solution, it typically exhibits a **pale green** hue.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation-Reduction (Redox) Aspect:**
 
 
• In this reaction, **Aluminium** undergoes **oxidation** as it loses **3 electrons** to become **Al3+** ions.
 
• The **Iron (Fe2+)** ions in the solution undergo **reduction** as they gain electrons to become neutral **Iron (Fe)** atoms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why other options are incorrect:**
 
 
• **Aluminium will get deposited:** This is incorrect because **Aluminium** is the one reacting and entering the solution as ions; it does not deposit as a solid from this specific reaction.
 
• **Blue solution will be formed:** This is incorrect because a **blue color** in inorganic salt solutions is usually characteristic of **Copper (Cu2+)** ions, not **Aluminium** or **Iron** ions. **Aluminium sulphate** solution is **colorless**.
 
• **There will be no reaction:** This is incorrect because a reaction **must occur** whenever a more reactive metal (Al) is introduced to a salt solution of a less reactive metal (Fe).
 
 
 
• **Safety and Observations:**
 
 
• The reaction is **exothermic**, meaning it releases a small amount of **heat energy**.
 
• In a laboratory setting, the **Aluminium** should be cleaned with **sandpaper** before the experiment to remove the **Aluminium oxide** layer that might slow down the initial reaction.

• **Cartilage** is a specialized type of **connective tissue** that is characterized by being compact, less vascular, and more flexible than bone.

• **Ligament**:
 
 
• A **ligament** is a very elastic and strong **connective tissue** that **connects bone to bone**.

• **Tendon**:

• **Hyaline Cartilage**: This is the most common type of cartilage in the body, providing **support and flexibility** to the **respiratory tract** and covering the ends of bones at **articulating joints**.

questions.question:
The work done in carrying a block of mass 30 kg to a height of ‘X’ m is 6000 J. What will be the value of X (in m)?
(Take the value of g = 10 { m/s}² )
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The work done in lifting an object against gravity is equal to the product of its **mass**, the **acceleration due to gravity**, and the **height** to which it is raised. This is expressed by the formula: **Work Done (W) = m * g * h**.
 
• In the given problem, the **mass (m)** of the block is **30 kg**, the **work done (W)** is **6000 J (Joules)**, and the **acceleration due to gravity (g)** is **10 m/s2**.
 
• Substituting the known values into the equation: **6000 = 30 * 10 * X**. Here, **X** represents the height (h) in **meters**.
 
• Simplifying the right side of the equation: **6000 = 300 * X**. To find the value of **X**, we divide the total work done by the product of mass and gravity: **X = 6000 / 300**.
 
• By performing the division, we get **X = 20**. Therefore, the block was carried to a height of **20 meters**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 20.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work Done:** In physics, work is said to be done when a **force** acts upon an object to cause a **displacement**. It is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it has magnitude but no direction. The **SI unit** of work is the **Joule (J)**, named after the English physicist **James Prescott Joule**.
 
• **Gravitational Potential Energy:** When work is done to lift an object to a certain height, the energy expended is stored in the object as **Gravitational Potential Energy (GPE)**. The amount of GPE an object possesses depends on its **mass** and its **height** relative to a reference point (usually the ground).
 
• **Acceleration due to Gravity:** On the surface of the **Earth**, the standard value for **g** is approximately **9.8 m/s2**. however, for ease of calculation in many competitive exams, it is often rounded to **10 m/s2** as specified in this question.
 
• **Units of Measurement:** It is crucial to ensure all units are in the **SI system** (Standard International) before calculation. Mass should be in **kilograms (kg)**, distance/height in **meters (m)**, and work in **Joules (J)**. If the mass were given in grams, it would need to be converted (**1 kg = 1000 g**) to get the correct result in Joules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nature of Work:** Work can be **positive**, **negative**, or **zero**. When the force and displacement are in the same direction (like lifting a block), the work is **positive**. If the force is perpendicular to the displacement (like carrying a bucket horizontally), the work done by gravity is **zero**.
 
• **Energy Conservation:** The **Law of Conservation of Energy** states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed. In this scenario, **chemical energy** from the person doing the work is converted into the **potential energy** of the block.
 
• **Force Component:** The force required to lift the block at a constant speed is equal to its weight, which is calculated as **Weight (F) = m * g**. For this problem, the weight is **30 kg * 10 m/s2 = 300 Newtons (N)**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following sounds has the lowest pitch?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A man’s deep voice (100 Hz)**__.

__
 
• **Pitch** is a characteristic of sound that allows the brain to perceive the **frequency** of a sound wave. It determines how "shrill" or "deep" a sound is to the human ear.
 
• The **frequency** of a sound refers to the number of **vibrations per second**. It is measured in the unit **Hertz (Hz)**. A higher frequency results in a higher pitch, while a **lower frequency** results in a **lower pitch**.
 
• In the given options:
 
 
• **A tuning fork (512 Hz)**: This is a relatively high frequency used in **musical calibration** and **physics experiments**.
 
• **A man’s deep voice (100 Hz)**: This is the **lowest frequency** among the choices, indicating the **lowest pitch**. ***Hence, this is the correct option.***
 
• **A child’s voice (350 Hz)**: Children generally have **shorter vocal cords**, leading to a higher frequency and higher pitch than adult men.
 
• **A bird’s chirp (1500 Hz)**: This represents the **highest frequency** in the list, resulting in a very high-pitched, shrill sound.
 
 
 
• Sound waves with low frequencies have longer wavelengths, whereas high-pitched sounds have shorter wavelengths and **rapid vibrations**.
 
• The human ear interprets **100 Hz** as a deep, bass-heavy sound, which is typical for the **average adult male** during normal speech.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vocal Cord Physiology**:
 
 
• The **pitch** of a human voice is determined by the **length, mass, and tension** of the vocal cords. 
 
• **Adult Men**: Have vocal cords that are approximately **17 mm to 25 mm** in length. Because they are thicker and longer, they vibrate more slowly, producing **lower frequencies** (typically **85 to 155 Hz**).
 
• **Adult Women**: Have vocal cords between **12.5 mm and 17.5 mm**. Shorter and thinner cords vibrate faster, producing **higher frequencies** (typically **165 to 255 Hz**).
 
• **Children**: Have the shortest vocal cords, resulting in the **highest pitch** among humans.
 
 
 
• **Frequency Range**:
 
 
• The **audible range** for the human ear is generally between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**.
 
• Sounds below **20 Hz** are called **Infrasonic** sounds (e.g., produced by **elephants** or **whales**).
 
• Sounds above **20,000 Hz** are called **Ultrasonic** sounds (e.g., used by **bats** for navigation and in **medical ultrasound**).
 
 
 
• **Distinction between Pitch and Loudness**:
 
 
• **Pitch** depends solely on the **frequency** (number of vibrations).
 
• **Loudness** depends on the **amplitude** (maximum displacement) of the sound wave and is measured in **Decibels (dB)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wave Anatomy**: In a **waveform graph**, pitch is visualized by how close the **crests and troughs** are to each other. A **low-pitch sound** (like 100 Hz) has waves that are **widely spaced**.
 
• **Environmental Examples**: A **drum** produces a low-pitched sound due to its low-frequency vibration, whereas a **whistle** produces a high-pitched sound due to high-frequency air vibrations.
 
• **Musical Context**: In music, pitch is referred to as "notes." A **bass guitar** operates at low frequencies (low pitch), while a **flute** or **violin** operates at high frequencies (high pitch).
 
• **Tuning Fork**: A **512 Hz** tuning fork corresponds to the musical note **C5** (High C), which is significantly higher in pitch than the **fundamental frequency** of a male voice.

questions.question: Impurities are converted to compounds by adding refining agents in which type of refining method?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical method**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chemical method** of refining involves the introduction of specific substances known as **refining agents** or **reagents** into an impure material, usually a molten metal.
 
• These agents are chosen based on their ability to react selectively with the **impurities** present in the mixture without affecting the primary metal or substance.
 
• During this process, the **impurities** are chemically converted into stable **compounds** such as **slags**, **oxides**, or **insoluble precipitates**.
 
• Once these **compounds** are formed, they are easily separated from the refined substance due to differences in **physical state**, **density**, or **solubility**.
 
• For example, in steelmaking, **Oxygen** is used as a **refining agent** to oxidize **Carbon**, **Silicon**, and **Manganese** into gases or slag, effectively removing them from the iron.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical Method**:
 
 
• This refining technique relies on the difference in **physical properties** between the substance and its impurities, such as **boiling points**, **melting points**, or **solubility**.
 
• Common examples include **Distillation** (used for volatile metals like **Zinc** and **Mercury**), **Liquation** (used for low-melting metals like **Tin**), and **Zone Refining** (used for ultra-pure **Semiconductors** like **Silicon**).
 
• In these methods, impurities are not converted into new chemical compounds but are separated through **phase changes**.
 
 
 
• **Electro-chemical Method**:
 
 
• Also known as **Electrolytic Refining**, this process uses an **Electric Current** to purify metals.
 
• The impure metal acts as the **Anode**, and a thin strip of pure metal acts as the **Cathode**, both immersed in an **Electrolyte** solution containing metal ions.
 
• Under the influence of current, pure metal ions migrate to the **Cathode**, while impurities either dissolve in the solution or settle at the bottom as **Anode Mud** (often containing precious metals like **Gold** or **Silver**).
 
 
 
• **Ionic Method**:
 
 
• This generally refers to processes like **Ion Exchange** or refining in **Molten Salts**, where ions are exchanged between a liquid phase and a solid resin or across a membrane.
 
• It is widely used in **Water Purification** and the separation of **Rare Earth Elements** where chemical similarities make standard methods difficult.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Flux and Slag**: In chemical refining, a **Flux** is a **refining agent** added to the furnace to remove impurities. When the **Flux** reacts with the impurity, it forms a fusible mass called **Slag**, which floats on the surface of the molten metal.
 
• **Chemical Affinity**: The success of the **Chemical method** depends on the higher **chemical affinity** of the refining agent for the impurity than for the metal being refined.
 
• **Examples of Chemical Refining**:
 
 
• **Cupellation**: Used for refining **Silver** and **Gold** by removing **Lead** as an oxide.
 
• **Bessemerization**: A historical **chemical method** for mass-producing steel by blowing air through molten pig iron to oxidize impurities.
 
• **Oxidative Refining**: Used for **Copper** and **Lead** where air or oxygen is used to remove impurities like **Arsenic** and **Antimony**.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: How many contrasting characters were used by Mendel to formulate the laws of inheritance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gregor Johann Mendel**, widely regarded as the **Father of Genetics**, conducted his historic hybridization experiments on **garden peas (Pisum sativum)**.
 
• He performed these experiments for a period of **seven years**, specifically from **1856 to 1863**.
 
• Mendel specifically selected **7 pairs of contrasting characters** (traits) to study the patterns of inheritance. ***Hence, the correct answer is 7.***
 
• These characters were chosen because they existed in two distinct, easily identifiable forms, such as **tall** or **dwarf** plants, which allowed for clear observation of results.
 
• Based on his observations of how these traits were passed from one generation to the next, he formulated the fundamental **Laws of Inheritance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Choice of Experimental Material**: Mendel chose the **garden pea (Pisum sativum)** for several reasons:
 
 
• The plant has a **short life cycle**, allowing for results to be seen quickly across multiple generations.
 
• It produces a **large number of offspring** (seeds) in a single generation, providing a sufficient **numerical value** for statistical analysis.
 
• Peas are naturally **self-pollinating**, but **cross-pollination** can be easily achieved manually.
 
 
 
• **Laws of Inheritance**: Mendel’s work led to three primary principles:
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**: In a heterozygote, one trait will conceal the presence of another trait for the same characteristic.
 
• **Law of Segregation**: During gamete formation, the alleles for each gene segregate from each other so that each gamete carries only one allele for each gene.
 
• **Law of Independent Assortment**: Genes for different traits can segregate independently during the formation of gametes.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**: Mendel presented his findings at the **Natural History Society of Brunn** in **1865**, and they were published in **1866**. However, his work remained largely unrecognized until its **rediscovery in 1900** by **Hugo de Vries**, **Carl Correns**, and **Erich von Tschermak**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Mendel studied the following **7 contrasting characters**, each having a **dominant** and a **recessive** trait:
 
 
• **Stem Height**: The dominant trait is **Tall** and the recessive is **Dwarf**.
 
• **Flower Color**: The dominant trait is **Violet** (or Purple) and the recessive is **White**.
 
• **Flower Position**: The dominant trait is **Axial** (along the stem) and the recessive is **Terminal** (at the tip).
 
• **Pod Shape**: The dominant trait is **Full (Inflated)** and the recessive is **Constricted**.
 
• **Pod Color**: The dominant trait is **Green** and the recessive is **Yellow**.
 
• **Seed Shape**: The dominant trait is **Round** and the recessive is **Wrinkled**.
 
• **Seed Color**: The dominant trait is **Yellow** and the recessive is **Green**.
 
 
 
• It is crucial to note the difference between pod and seed color; for **pods**, **green** is dominant, whereas for **seeds**, **yellow** is dominant.
 
• Mendel used **true-breeding lines** (pure-breeding) for all **7 characters** to ensure consistency in his **P (parental) generation**.

questions.question: The molecular mass of carbon dioxide is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**44 amu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **molecular mass** of a chemical compound is calculated by summing the **atomic masses** of every individual atom present in its **chemical formula**.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide** is represented by the chemical formula **CO2**, which indicates that one molecule of the gas contains **one atom** of **Carbon** and **two atoms** of **Oxygen**.
 
• The **atomic mass** of **Carbon (C)** is approximately **12.01 amu** (atomic mass units), which is typically rounded to **12 amu** for standard educational calculations.
 
• The **atomic mass** of **Oxygen (O)** is approximately **15.99 amu**, which is standardly rounded to **16 amu**.
 
• To find the **molecular mass** of **CO2**, the calculation is as follows: (**1 atom of Carbon** x **12 amu**) + (**2 atoms of Oxygen** x **16 amu**) = **12** + **32** = **44 amu**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 44 amu.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical Properties of CO2**: **Carbon Dioxide** is a **colorless** and **odorless** gas at **standard temperature and pressure**. It is approximately **1.5 times** as dense as **air** and occurs naturally in **Earth's atmosphere** as a trace gas.
 
• **Chemical Nature**: It consists of a **carbon atom** covalently double-bonded to two **oxygen atoms**. It is a linear molecule and is **non-polar** despite the polarity of the individual **C-O bonds** due to its symmetrical shape.
 
• **Dry Ice**: Below a temperature of **-78.5 degrees Celsius**, **Carbon Dioxide** undergoes **sublimation**, changing directly from a gas to a **solid** form known as **dry ice**, which is widely used for **refrigeration** and cooling.
 
• **Biological Importance**: **Carbon Dioxide** is a vital component of the **carbon cycle**. It is consumed by **plants**, **algae**, and **cyanobacteria** during the process of **photosynthesis** to produce energy and **oxygen**.
 
• **Industrial Uses**: It is used in the **food industry** to provide **carbonation** in soft drinks, in **fire extinguishers** as it does not support **combustion**, and in **welding** as an inert **shielding gas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (amu)**: This is a **unit of mass** used to express **atomic** and **molecular weights**. It is defined as exactly **1/12th** of the mass of an atom of **Carbon-12**. In modern terminology, it is often referred to as the **unified atomic mass unit (u)** or the **Dalton (Da)**.
 
• **Molar Mass vs. Molecular Mass**: While **molecular mass** is the mass of a single molecule (measured in **amu**), **molar mass** is the mass of one **mole** of the substance (**6.022 x 10^23** molecules), expressed in **grams per mole (g/mol)**. For **CO2**, the **molar mass** is **44.01 g/mol**.
 
• **Comparison with other gases**:
 
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**: Molecular mass is **28 amu** (12 + 16).
 
• **Oxygen Gas (O2)**: Molecular mass is **32 amu** (16 x 2).
 
• **Nitrogen Gas (N2)**: Molecular mass is **28 amu** (14 x 2).
 
• **Methane (CH4)**: Molecular mass is **16 amu** (12 + 4).
 
 
 
• **Greenhouse Effect**: **CO2** is a primary **greenhouse gas**. Since the **Industrial Revolution**, human activities such as **deforestation** and the burning of **fossil fuels** have significantly increased its **atmospheric concentration**, contributing to **global warming**.
</ul

questions.question: Two resistors of 2 Omega and X Omega are connected in series to a 10 V battery. If the current flowing through the resistors is 2 A, then what will be the value of X (in Ohm)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In a **series circuit**, the **equivalent resistance** (R_eq) is the sum of all individual resistances connected in the path. In this case, the total resistance is given by the formula **R_eq = R1 + R2**.
 
• According to **Ohm's Law**, the relationship between **Voltage (V)**, **Current (I)**, and **Resistance (R)** is defined by the equation **V = I * R**.
 
• Given the **Voltage (V)** is **10 V** and the **Current (I)** is **2 A**, we can calculate the total resistance of the circuit using the formula **R_eq = V / I**. Substituting the values: **10 / 2 = 5 Ohm**. ***Hence, the total resistance of the circuit is 5 Ohm.***
 
• We are provided with one resistor of **2 Ohm** and another unknown resistor **X Ohm** connected in series. Therefore, **2 + X = 5**.
 
• Solving for **X**, we subtract 2 from 5: **X = 5 - 2 = 3 Ohm**. ***Hence, the value of the unknown resistor X is 3.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ohm's Law:** Discovered by the **German physicist Georg Simon Ohm** in **1827**, it states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points, provided physical conditions like **temperature** remain constant.
 
• **Series Combination:** In a series connection, there is only **one path** for the flow of electric current. Consequently, the **current (I)** remains the **same** through all components, while the total **potential difference (Voltage)** is distributed across them.
 
• **Parallel Combination:** In a parallel circuit, components are connected across the same two nodes. Here, the **potential difference (V)** across each resistor remains the **same**, but the **total current** is the sum of currents through each branch. The formula for equivalent resistance is **1/R_eq = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + ... + 1/Rn**.
 
• **Resistance:** It is the property of a conductor to **oppose the flow of electric current**. The **SI unit** of resistance is the **Ohm**, symbolized by the Greek letter **Omega (Ω)**.

questions.question: The image formed by a concave lens for an object at infinity is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual, erect, and point-sized**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **concave lens** is also known as a **diverging lens** because it diverges the light rays that pass through it parallel to its **principal axis**.
 
• When an **object is placed at infinity**, the incident rays are parallel to the **principal axis**. After **refraction** through the concave lens, these rays appear to diverge from the **principal focus (F1)** located on the same side as the object.
 
• The image formed under these conditions is **virtual**, meaning it cannot be obtained on a screen, and it is **erect** (upright).
 
• In terms of size, the image is **highly diminished** or **point-sized** at the **focus**.
 
• This behavior is consistent regardless of the **focal length** of the concave lens, as its primary function is to spread out light rays.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Image Formation for Other Positions:** Unlike convex lenses, a **concave lens** always produces a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image, regardless of the **object's distance** from the lens. If the object is moved from **infinity** closer to the **optical center**, the image moves from the **focus** toward the **optical center** and increases slightly in size, but remains smaller than the object.
 
• **Lens Formula and Magnification:** The relationship between object distance (u), image distance (v), and focal length (f) is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**. For a concave lens, the **magnification (m = v/u)** is always **positive** and **less than 1**, confirming the image is always **erect** and **diminished**.
 
• **Sign Convention:** According to the **Cartesian sign convention**, the **focal length** of a **concave lens** is always taken as **negative**. Similarly, the **image distance (v)** is also **negative** because the virtual image is formed on the left side of the lens (the same side as the object).
 
• **Practical Applications:** Concave lenses are widely used in **spectacles** to correct **Myopia** (nearsightedness), in **peepholes** of house doors to provide a wide view of people outside, and in **flashlights** to spread the light beam over a larger area.
 
• **Power of Lens:** The **power** of a concave lens is expressed in **Dioptres (D)** and is always **negative**, calculated as the reciprocal of the focal length in meters (**P = 1/f**).

• The **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** is a membrane-bound network of tubules that lacks **ribosomes** on its surface, distinguishing it from the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**.

• **Intracellular Transport**: The **ER** serves as a channel for the **transport of materials**, particularly **proteins**, between different regions of the **cytoplasm** or between the **cytoplasm** and the **nucleus**.
 
• **Biochemical Framework**: The **ER** provides a large surface area for various **biochemical activities** and **enzymatic reactions** necessary for the cell's survival.

questions.question: The direction of the magnetic field at the centre of a current-carrying circular loop is determined by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right-Hand Thumb Rule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**, also frequently referred to as **Maxwell's Corkscrew Rule**, is the primary method used to determine the direction of the **magnetic field** associated with a **current-carrying conductor**.
 
• When applying this rule to a **circular loop**, if we curl the fingers of the **right hand** in the direction of the **current** flowing through the loop, the extended **thumb** points toward the direction of the **magnetic field** at the **centre** of the loop.
 
• Conversely, if the **thumb** is pointed in the direction of the **current** along any small segment of the wire, the **curl of the fingers** shows the direction of the **magnetic field lines** encircling that segment.
 
• At the **centre** of the **circular loop**, all the **magnetic field lines** produced by different segments of the wire aid each other, resulting in a **magnetic field** that is **perpendicular** to the plane of the loop.
 
• If the **current** flows in a **clockwise** direction when viewed from one side, the **magnetic field** at the **centre** is directed **inwards** (away from the observer); if the **current** flows **counter-clockwise**, the field is directed **outwards** (towards the observer). ***Hence, the correct answer is Right-Hand Thumb Rule.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming’s Left-Hand Rule**:
 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of the **force (motion)** acting on a **current-carrying conductor** placed within an external **magnetic field**.
 
• In this rule, the **forefinger** represents the **magnetic field**, the **middle finger** represents the **current**, and the **thumb** represents the **force** or **motion** of the conductor. It is the basis for the working of **electric motors**.
 
 
 
• **Fleming’s Right-Hand Rule**:
 
 
• This rule is primarily used to identify the direction of the **induced current** when a conductor moves inside a **magnetic field**.
 
• The **thumb** indicates the direction of **motion**, the **forefinger** points in the direction of the **magnetic field**, and the **middle finger** points in the direction of the **induced current**. This principle is utilized in **electric generators**.
 
 
 
• **Lenz’s Law**:
 
 
• Formulated by **Heinrich Lenz** in **1834**, this law states that the direction of an **induced electromotive force (EMF)** is always such that it opposes the change in **magnetic flux** that produced it.
 
• It is a qualitative law that follows the principle of **conservation of energy**.
 
 
 
• **Magnitude of Magnetic Field in a Loop**:
 
 
• The **strength** of the **magnetic field (B)** at the **centre** of a **circular loop** of **radius (R)** carrying a **current (I)** is given by the formula **B = (μ₀ * I) / (2 * R)**.
 
• Here, **μ₀** represents the **permeability of free space**, which has a constant value of approximately **4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A**.
 
• The **magnetic field** is **directly proportional** to the **current** and **inversely proportional** to the **radius** of the loop. If the loop has **N** turns, the field strength is multiplied by **N**.

⇒ 437 + 386

**__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

Standard order for operations: Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Mathematical Sign Interchange

Always rewrite the complete expression after replacing all specified symbols before starting any arithmetic calculations.

Unit Digit Method

questions.question: Which national park was declared India’s 58th Tiger Reserve in March 2025?

• The notification was issued by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** following the final approval from the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**.
 
• This declaration makes **Madhya Pradesh** the state with the highest number of tiger reserves in India, bringing its total count to **8** (including Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Panna, Pench, Satpura, Sanjay-Dubri, and Veerangana Durgavati).
 
• The initiative is part of a broader conservation strategy to reintroduce and stabilize tiger populations in the **Gwalior-Chambal** region and create a functional wildlife corridor connecting **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve** in **Rajasthan** with **Kuno National Park** and **Madhav National Park**.

• The **NTCA** is a statutory body under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**, constituted under the enabling provisions of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, as amended in **2006**.
 
• It provides statutory authority to **Project Tiger** and oversees the management and protection of tiger reserves across various states.

• According to the **2022 Tiger Census**, India is home to approximately **3,682 tigers**, which constitutes about **75%** of the global wild tiger population.

• The park is situated in the **Vindhyan Hills** and features a diverse ecosystem consisting of **dry deciduous forests** and flat grasslands.
 
• It is home to the **Sakhya Sagar** and **Madhav Sagar** lakes, which are designated **Ramsar Sites**, providing a crucial habitat for migratory birds and crocodiles.

• Being declared a **Tiger Reserve** allows the park to receive dedicated funding and specialized protection forces under **Project Tiger**, enhancing anti-poaching measures and habitat management.

• It focuses on removing **administrative bottlenecks** that have historically led to legal disputes, mismanagement of funds, and a lack of proper support for athletes at the **grassroots level**.

• **Anti-Doping and Ethics**: The act reinforces compliance with **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** and **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** protocols, making the federations directly responsible for the **ethical conduct** of their members.
